Divorce (Biblical Grounds)
duh-VORS
noun phrase (Christian ethics)
The biblical doctrine of the lawful grounds for divorce. The Reformed-confessional position (Westminster Confession XXIV) holds that there are two biblical grounds: adultery (Matthew 5:32; 19:9) and irremediable desertion by an unbelieving spouse (1 Corinthians 7:15). Marriage is a lifelong covenant designed to be permanent; divorce is permitted only on these grounds.

📖 Biblical Definition

The biblical doctrine of the lawful grounds for divorce. The Reformed-confessional position (Westminster Confession XXIV.5-6) holds that marriage is a lifelong covenant designed by God to be permanent (Genesis 2:24; Matthew 19:6, what therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder), and that divorce is lawful only on two biblical grounds. (1) Adultery / sexual immorality: the Lord Jesus permits divorce for fornication (Greek porneia, sexual immorality; Matthew 5:32; 19:9, whosoever shall put away his wife, except it be for fornication, and shall marry another, committeth adultery). The innocent spouse may lawfully divorce the adulterous spouse. (2) Irremediable desertion by an unbelieving spouse: Paul permits the believing spouse to be released when the unbelieving spouse departs and will not be reconciled (1 Corinthians 7:15, But if the unbelieving depart, let him depart. A brother or a sister is not under bondage in such cases). The Westminster Confession (XXIV.6) summarizes: nothing but adultery, or such willful desertion as can no way be remedied by the church or civil magistrate, is cause sufficient of dissolving the bond of marriage. The patriarchal-Reformed reader holds the substantive Reformed-confessional doctrine: marriage is a lifelong covenant; divorce is a grave matter permitted only on the two biblical grounds; the no-fault divorce regime of the modern West (which permits divorce for any reason or no reason) contradicts the biblical doctrine and has been catastrophic for households, children, and the broader social order. The church is called to uphold the permanence of marriage, to counsel reconciliation wherever possible, to recognize the two biblical grounds where they genuinely obtain, and to minister the gospel of grace to those wounded by divorce.

DIVORCE (BIBLICAL GROUNDS), n. phr. (Christian ethics) The lawful grounds for divorce. Reformed-confessional position (Westminster XXIV.5-6): marriage is a lifelong covenant designed to be permanent (Genesis 2:24; Matthew 19:6); divorce lawful only on two grounds: (1) adultery / sexual immorality (Greek porneia; Matthew 5:32; 19:9 — the innocent spouse may lawfully divorce the adulterous); (2) irremediable desertion by an unbelieving spouse (1 Corinthians 7:15 — if the unbelieving depart, let him depart; a brother or a sister is not under bondage in such cases). Westminster XXIV.6: nothing but adultery, or such willful desertion as can no way be remedied by the church or civil magistrate, is cause sufficient of dissolving the bond of marriage. No-fault divorce contradicts the biblical doctrine.

📖 Key Scripture

Matthew 19:6 — "Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder."

Matthew 19:9 — "And I say unto you, Whosoever shall put away his wife, except it be for fornication, and shall marry another, committeth adultery: and whoso marrieth her which is put away doth commit adultery."

1 Corinthians 7:15 — "But if the unbelieving depart, let him depart. A brother or a sister is not under bondage in such cases: but God hath called us to peace."

Malachi 2:16 — "For the LORD, the God of Israel, saith that he hateth putting away: for one covereth violence with his garment, saith the LORD of hosts: therefore take heed to your spirit, that ye deal not treacherously."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The no-fault divorce regime (divorce for any reason or no reason) contradicts the biblical doctrine that marriage is a lifelong covenant dissolvable only on the two biblical grounds of adultery and irremediable desertion.

expand to see more

The no-fault divorce regime of the modern West contradicts the biblical doctrine at its foundation. The modern legal regime (beginning substantially with California's no-fault divorce law of 1969 and spreading throughout the Western world) permits divorce for any reason or no reason — irreconcilable differences, incompatibility, or simple unilateral desire. The biblical doctrine holds that marriage is a lifelong covenant designed by God to be permanent (Genesis 2:24; Matthew 19:6), dissolvable only on the two biblical grounds: adultery (Matthew 5:32; 19:9) and irremediable desertion by an unbelieving spouse (1 Corinthians 7:15). The LORD declares that He hates putting away (Malachi 2:16). The no-fault regime has been catastrophic: the dissolution of millions of households; the fatherlessness of vast numbers of children; the impoverishment of divorced women and children; the broader social disintegration that follows the collapse of marital permanence. The patriarchal-Reformed reader holds the substantive biblical doctrine: marriage is a lifelong covenant; divorce is a grave matter permitted only on the two biblical grounds; the church upholds the permanence of marriage, counsels reconciliation wherever possible, recognizes the two biblical grounds where they genuinely obtain, and ministers the gospel of grace to those wounded by the divorce culture.
